config: prompt-only (grammar removed), max_tokens=512, 3 models x 2 temps x 8 = 48
what_was_fixed: Validator: _parse_thinking_envelope now tolerates the model's NATIVE <think>...</think> channel as a closed reasoning envelope (was rejected as extra_prose). Genuine correctness fix, unit-tested. This removed a FALSE cause.

Grammar: thinking_tag_closed removed from the grammar lane (f4_family_grammar -> None). The f4_thinking_tag_diagnose probe showed the structural-tag </thinking> trigger never fires on the native <think> channel and drives generation into a runaway. Removed a SECOND false cause.
real_residual: Even prompt-only at max_tokens=512 with the corrected validator, 42/48 samples are thinking_tag_unclosed and 42/48 hit finish_reason=length: the reasoning models do not reliably CLOSE their <think> reasoning within the token budget at temp 0/0.3. That is the dominant cause, not the validator or grammar. The single empty-<think></think> success in the diagnosis was not representative.
verdict: thinking_tag_closed is NOT salvaged. #2 corrected two false causes (validator strictness, grammar backfire) and isolated the true one (reasoning models do not close their native channel in budget). It stays a documented F-4 residual and remains OUT of the clean reliability lane. Break rate moved only ~100% -> ~88%, confirming the dominant cause was the reasoning-length problem all along.
